-- Business rule: a record cannot be closed after the last time it was touched,
-- because closing it IS touching it.
--
-- This is the test that failed on the raw data. The naive version, with no
-- tolerance, returns 7,886 rows out of 690,427. Before weakening the test I
-- checked the magnitude of the violation:
--
--   select min(d), median(d), max(d) from (
--     select (epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at)) as d
--     from stg_service_requests where closed_at > last_modified_at)
--
--   min = 1.0, median = 1.0, max = 1.0   (seconds)
--
-- Every single violation is exactly one second, across all nine service types.
-- That is a write-ordering artifact in the City's own system, where the closure
-- timestamp and the modified timestamp are stamped by different statements, not
-- a corrupted record. A one-second skew changes no closure duration that this
-- project reports, since the smallest unit any mart uses is a minute.
--
-- So the rule is kept but given a two-second tolerance, which still catches a
-- genuine ordering break while not firing on the clock artifact. The defect is
-- recorded as defect 5 in docs/DATA_QUALITY.md with its row count, rather than
-- being silently dropped.

select
    sr_number,
    closed_at,
    last_modified_at,
    epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at) as seconds_after_last_modified
from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests"
where closed_at is not null
  and last_modified_at is not null
  and epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at) > 2

-- Business rule: if the City says a request is Completed, there has to be a
-- closure timestamp, otherwise the request cannot be counted in any wait-time
-- number and the closure rate reported on the dashboard is wrong.
--
-- This matters more than it looks. mart_service_type_summary publishes
-- closure_rate as requests_measurable / requests_total. If Completed requests
-- can be unmeasurable, that ratio understates performance by an unknown amount
-- and nobody looking at the dashboard can tell.
--
-- The rule is asserted with a tolerance of zero on purpose: 0 rows in this
-- slice, and if the City ever starts publishing completions without timestamps
-- the closure_rate column needs a caveat before it ships, not after.

select
    sr_number,
    service_type,
    status,
    status_raw,
    closed_at
from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests"
where status = 'Completed'
  and closed_at is null

-- Business rule: the ward mart must not lose or invent requests. Its
-- requests_total summed over all rows has to equal the count of ward-attributed
-- requests in the fact model.
--
-- Worth asserting because the mart has a join to stg_wards. An inner join on a
-- ward that was missing from the seed would quietly drop a whole ward's
-- volume, the chart would still render, and the only symptom would be a
-- citywide total that is slightly too low.
--
-- Allows a difference of exactly zero.

with mart_total as (
    select sum(requests_total) as n from "chicago311"."main_marts"."mart_ward_service_performance"
),
fact_total as (
    select count(*) as n from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests" where ward is not null
)
select
    mart_total.n as mart_rows,
    fact_total.n as fact_rows,
    mart_total.n - fact_total.n as difference
from mart_total
cross join fact_total
where mart_total.n != fact_total.n

-- Business rule: a service request cannot be closed before it was opened.
--
-- Chicago's 311 system records closure when a crew files completion, so a
-- closed_date earlier than created_date means either a backdated entry or a
-- bad merge. If it ever appears, the median wait in every mart is silently
-- pulled down, so this is a hard failure rather than a warning.
--
-- Status at time of writing: 0 rows in the 2023-2024 slice. The test stays
-- because the defect is present in other years of this dataset and would
-- arrive with a wider extract window.

select
    sr_number,
    created_at,
    closed_at,
    days_to_close_raw
from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests"
where closed_at is not null
  and closed_at < created_at

-- Business rule about the pipeline itself: staging renames and types, it does
-- not filter. If stg_service_requests has fewer rows than raw.service_requests
-- then a cast or a trim is dropping records, and every data-quality count in
-- docs/DATA_QUALITY.md is being measured against an already-thinned table.
--
-- This is the test that makes the data-quality documentation trustworthy. The
-- counts in that file are taken from staging, and they are only honest if
-- staging is lossless.

with staged as (
    select count(*) as n from "chicago311"."main_staging"."stg_service_requests"
),
raw_rows as (
    select count(*) as n from "chicago311"."raw"."service_requests"
)
select
    staged.n as staging_rows,
    raw_rows.n as raw_rows,
    staged.n - raw_rows.n as difference
from staged
cross join raw_rows
where staged.n != raw_rows.n

-- Business rule: Chicago has 50 wards, numbered 1 to 50. A ward of 0, 51 or
-- 999 is not a place, and a ward-level mart built on one would show a bar for
-- a district that does not exist.
--
-- The clean_ward macro is what enforces this, by nulling anything outside the
-- range instead of passing it through. This test is the guard on that macro:
-- if someone edits clean_ward and widens the range, this fails.
--
-- Checked in both directions. First, no out-of-range ward survives into the
-- fact model. Second, every non-null ward in the fact model exists in the
-- ward dimension, which the relationships test also covers but which is
-- cheap to assert here against the literal range.

select
    sr_number,
    ward_raw,
    ward,
    'ward outside 1-50' as failure_reason
from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests"
where ward is not null
  and (ward < 1 or ward > 50)

union all

select
    sr_number,
    ward_raw,
    ward,
    'ward not present in ward dimension' as failure_reason
from "chicago311"."main_intermediate"."int_service_requests" r
where r.ward is not null
  and not exists (select 1 from "chicago311"."main_staging"."stg_wards" w where w.ward = r.ward)
